question: On a frozen Montreal archive image corpus, does one update using fresh pixels-only caption feedback improve paired French/English visual-query retrieval over the same encoder without feedback?

hypotheses.prediction: Fresh-caption GRF improves mean paired-intent nDCG@10 over no-feedback image retrieval by at least 0.05 absolute, with a 95% interval excluding zero and no established language decline greater than 0.03.
hypotheses.falsification: The upper primary interval is below the practical threshold, or a material language regression is established; inadequate precision or reference quality is inconclusive.

paper.title: A Little More Like This: Text-to-Image Retrieval with Vision-Language Models Using Relevance Feedback

metrics: native French and English deltas and intervals
protocol.label_policy: Independent human visual-intent/image relevance, complete small-corpus judgments, bilingual wording equivalence, blind second heldout reviewer and adjudication. No model-generated gold.
pending: reviewed shared corpus and family metric adapter
independent development and protected new heldout intents

limitations: Preparation only: registering this study launches no inference or evaluation.
The numerical kernel uses synthetic vectors and has no human benchmark scores.
Paper benchmark gains do not establish gains on archival images or French queries.
Legacy captions have unknown input lineage; replacement contrasts cannot isolate caption-model quality.
This study addresses visible concepts, not exact historical place/date attribution or OCR.
Delivery-image processing does not establish preserved-master processing quality.
Production resources and app behavior remain independent.
